To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Calcium signalling is an important process in plants, and mathematical and computational modelling has been employed to help understand it.
calcium signalling in plant cells is a complex system that can be modelled and that models can be useful in understanding the system.

(i) the dynamics of calcium signalling in guard cells are determined by the interplay between the kinetics of ion channels and the properties of the cytosol; (ii) the calcium signatures that arise during stomatal closure can be reproduced in silico using a simple model of calcium signalling; (iii) a mathematical model can be used to investigate the effect of the cytoplasmic calcium buffer, calsequestrin, on stomatal closure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the complex patterns of calcium signals are generated and how these patterns are used to regulate downstream processes.
developing and testing mathematical models that can capture the complex dynamics of calcium signalling and help to elucidate the mechanisms that underpin these phenomena.
the development of models of plant calcium signalling that are both biophysically plausible and able to reproduce experimental observations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current state of the art of plant calcium signalling modelling is that it is in its infancy.
we are still at an early stage in understanding the mechanisms of plant calcium signalling.
we have a good understanding of some aspects of calcium dynamics, but that there is still much to learn.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and applied mathematical models to calcium signalling in plants that have been useful for understanding the mechanisms that give raise to complex calcium signatures.
the models are useful, but the systems are complex, and we are still a long way from a full understanding.
the modelling of plant signalling systems is an exciting field of research, with many open questions and challenges.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of calcium dynamics in plants requires a multi-scale modelling approach.
the systems biology approach is a powerful tool for investigating the complex and poorly understood calcium signalling pathways of plants.
calcium signalling in plants is a highly complex system and that the interplay between different mechanisms and the resulting emergent behaviour can be difficult to predict.
